# NET-003: SSH is not open to anywhere when a private path exists

- **Group:** Firewall and exposure
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

SSH open to the whole internet draws constant brute force traffic and exposes every future sshd flaw. When Tailscale is running, SSH can stay reachable over the tailnet and be closed publicly. This check needs the Tailscale facts: without them the result is unknown, because closing public SSH without a proven private path is how people lock themselves out.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo ufw status verbose | grep -E '22|OpenSSH'; tailscale status; ss -tlnp | grep sshd
```

## How to fix it

Allow SSH on tailscale0 and from one explicit source, prove a login over the tailnet from a new session, then delete the public SSH rule

## What a fix can break

Deleting the public rule before the tailnet path works locks you out; a logged out Tailscale node makes every tailscale0 rule dead (see TS-001).
